items.title: Island Paradise of Mauritius Has Sun, Beaches and Too Many Dogs
items.excerpt: Mauritius, a popular tourist destination off southern Africa, has become overrun with strays. With more and more residents chased and attacked, many are fed up.

items.title: Judges in Israel Suggest Dropping Key Corruption Case Against Netanyahu
items.excerpt: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is accused of bribery, fraud and breach of trust in a long-running trial that has divided the country. He denies all wrongdoing.

items.title: Hungary Threw Open Its Secret Police Files. Let the Finger Pointing Begin.
items.excerpt: The communist-era files have exposed the vast network of informants that kept Hungary in the Soviet orbit. But how reliable are they?

items.title: South African President Wins Reprieve From ‘Farmgate’ Impeachment Investigation
items.excerpt: A court threw out a report suggesting that Cyril Ramaphosa may have tried to conceal the theft of more than half a million dollars of U.S. currency.

items.title: How an Iranian Ally Gained the Upper Hand in Yemen’s War
items.excerpt: The Iran-backed Houthis are on a winning streak, securing strategic territory as they fight Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies in an asymmetrical war of attrition.

items.title: Defending Aden, Yemen’s Holdout Against the Houthis
items.excerpt: The war in Iran has reignited Yemen’s decade-old civil war. Saudi-backed troops are scrambling to defend against advancing Houthi fighters as the wounded are taken to the port city of Aden, the government’s provisional capital.

items.title: Libyan Forces Threaten Retaliation Over Ukraine’s Attack on Russian Ships
items.excerpt: The Ukrainian drone strike off Libya’s coast killed two Libyan naval officers, according to the forces controlling the country’s east.

items.title: Mexico Investigates Possible Cartel Links of Prosecutor Who Aided C.I.A.
items.excerpt: The prosecutor recently fled to the United States after Mexico issued a warrant over his involvement with the C.I.A. Now authorities are investigating him for suspected cartel collusion.

items.title: 3 Dead and Many More Trapped in Indonesian Mine After Heavy Rainfall
items.excerpt: At least 23 workers are believed to have been stuck inside the illegal mine since Monday, after its narrow shaft flooded.

items.title: North Korea Kicks Out Swiss Diplomats in Spat Linked to Ukraine War
items.excerpt: The move followed Switzerland’s decision to impose sanctions on an international youth camp in North Korea, which is accused of hosting Ukrainian children for indoctrination.

items.title: Solomon Islands Enters Security Treaty With Australia, in a Blow to China
items.excerpt: A 2022 Solomon Islands agreement with China had raised concerns it would enable Beijing to establish a military presence on the Pacific island. The new accord precludes such bases.

items.title: Colombia’s Leader Blames ‘Terrorist Attack’ for Power Outages
items.excerpt: The blackouts follow a string of violent episodes attributed to Colombia’s armed traffickers, as the country’s new president cracks down on the groups.

items.title: 2 Men Charged After Break-In at Prince William and Kate’s Country Home
items.excerpt: Prosecutors said the two men, who appeared in court on Wednesday, had climbed a drainpipe to break into the royals’ country retreat in Norfolk.

items.title: Radio Offers Russian Troops Classic Rock, Nostalgia — and Pleas to Surrender
items.excerpt: What seem like frontline Russian radio stations are actually a Ukrainian psychological operation, hoping to sow despair among the Kremlin’s soldiers.

items.title: Africa C.D.C. Chief Faces Turmoil Over Management Amid Ebola Crisis
items.excerpt: Scrutiny has fallen on Dr. Jean Kaseya, the director general of the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, after reports of staff intimidation and mismanagement of funds.

items.title: Gordon Ramsay to Host Revival of BBC’s ‘Top Gear’
items.excerpt: The British car show “Top Gear” paused production three years ago and is returning with a new host in 2028, the BBC said.

items.title: Road Fire Near Cairo Kills Dozens After Petroleum-Laden Truck Crashes
items.excerpt: The blaze killed at least 31 and injured at least 21 near Giza, beside the Nile River, officials said.

items.title: Study Hard, Get Ahead?
items.excerpt: The broken promise of upward mobility through education is sparking youth protests around the world.

items.title: Lukoil to Sell Foreign Assets, but Not to Kushner and Witkoff Associates
items.excerpt: Valuable properties belonging to the Russian energy giant will be sold to an American-led consortium. But Middle Eastern business contacts of the two Trump envoys pulled out because of political winds.

items.title: Opposition Makes Progress Toward Ousting Netanyahu, Party Leader Says
items.excerpt: Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, has set Dec. 6 as the deadline to form a new Israeli government. His ally, Avigdor Liberman, said Mr. Eisenkot was on track.

items.title: How to Celebrate Thanksgiving as an Expat
items.excerpt: From turkeys delivered on motorbikes to foie gras on the table, many American expatriates have adapted the traditional meal to their environs.

items.title: Thomas Markle Indicted in US on Charges of Possession of Child Sexual Abuse Materials
items.excerpt: Mr. Markle, 82, was indicted by a grand jury in Los Angeles and is expected to be arraigned in the coming weeks, prosecutors said.

items.title: Trump Administration Pauses Joint Operations With Ecuador
items.excerpt: The administration has halted military operations while it investigates an operation by Ecuadorean forces that killed an accused gang leader.

items.title: ‘Saturday Night Live’ Is Coming to France
items.excerpt: A French adaptation of the American sketch comedy institution will premiere next month on the premium channel Canal+. It comes as a British version is hitting a stride.

items.title: National Security vs. the Stock Market
items.excerpt: President Trump swept aside concerns about possible espionage when he lobbied Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive.

items.title: Iraq’s Prime Minister Aims to Wrest More Power From Kurdistan Region
items.excerpt: Ali al-Zaidi, who just scored a symbolic victory against a powerful Iran-backed militia, has now moved to assert control over Kurdish border crossings and oil resources.

items.title: Houthi Attack on Skyscraper in Saudi Capital Wounds 11, Officials Say
items.excerpt: The people were wounded in the strike on a building in Riyadh, the Saudi authorities said. The Iran-backed militia and Saudi Arabia have been exchanging escalating attacks for weeks.

items.title: A Lion on the Loose Near Istanbul? Not So Fast.
items.excerpt: Blurry surveillance footage spurred a frantic search — until the Turkish authorities said it was unclear whether the animal was the feline.

items.title: Trump’s Nvidia Push Shows Companies’ Importance in Global Economic War
items.excerpt: Presidents before him have bailed out companies in times of national crisis. Mr. Trump went further: He staked the fortunes of the United States on those of a favored chief executive.

items.title: Murder Charge Reinstated for French Police Officer in Teen’s Shooting
items.excerpt: The killing of Nahel Merzouk, 17, sparked nationwide unrest. The case against the officer accused of involvement has undergone repeated twists and turns.
